ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The ports in the figure are P and Q. From terminal P to the right, a 4 Ω resistor is first connected in series, reaching a node; from this node downward there is a 4 Ω resistor connected to the bottom common node Q. This node continues to the right through a 2 Ω resistor in series and then connects to the upper end of a 125 mH inductor, with the lower end of the 125 mH inductor connected to Q. On the right side there is another 1 mH inductor magnetically coupled with it, and it forms a loop with a 50 μF capacitor; the mutual inductance is marked as 5 mH, and the upper ends of both coils have dot markings. Reasoning: According to the given angular frequency ω = 5000 rad/s, the impedance of the 125 mH winding is jωL1 = j(5000)(0.125) = j625 Ω; the impedance of the 1 mH winding is jωL2 = j(5000)(0.001) = j5 Ω; the impedance of the 50 μF capacitor is 1/(jωC) = -j/(5000×50×10^-6) = -j4 Ω; the mutual inductance impedance is jωM = j(5000)(0.005) = j25 Ω. The total impedance of the secondary loop is Z2 = j5 - j4 = j1 Ω. The mutual inductance term reflected to the 125 mH primary side is (ωM)^2/Z2 = 25^2/(j1) = 625/j = -j625 Ω. Therefore, the equivalent impedance of the 125 mH branch is j625 + (-j625) = 0 Ω, equivalent to this branch being short-circuited to Q. Thus looking in from P, there is first a 4 Ω series resistor; after that, from the node to Q there are 4 Ω and 2 Ω in parallel, because the inductor branch after the 2 Ω has already been equivalent to a short circuit. Therefore Zth = 4 + (4 || 2) = 4 + (4×2)/(4+2) = 4 + 8/6 = 5.333... Ω, rounded to 2 decimal places as 5.33 Ω.

method.method_draft: Compute at ω=5000 rad/s: jωL1=j625 for the 125 mH winding, jωL2=j5 for the 1 mH winding, ZC=-j4 for the 50 μF capacitor, and jωM=j25. The secondary loop impedance is Z2=j5-j4=j1, so the reflected term is (ωM)^2/Z2=625/(j1)=-j625. Thus the effective impedance of the 125 mH primary branch becomes j625-j625=0 Ω, i.e. that branch behaves as a short to Q. The port network then becomes a 4 Ω series resistor from P followed by a node where 4 Ω is in parallel with 2 Ω to Q. Hence Zth=4+(4||2)=4+8/6=5.333..., rounded to 5.33 Ω.

method.method_draft: Apply a 1 V phasor test source between P and Q, with Q as ground. Let Va be the node after the first 4 Ω resistor, Vb be the top of the 125 mH inductor, i1 be the current in the 125 mH winding, and i2 be the secondary loop current. Use the coupled-coil equations: Vb=jωL1 i1+jωM i2 and 0=jωM i1+(jωL2+1/(jωC))i2. Substituting ω=5000, L1=125 mH, L2=1 mH, C=50 μF, M=5 mH gives 0=j25 i1+j1 i2, so i2=-25i1, and therefore Vb=j625i1+j25(-25i1)=0. Now solve the resistive KCL equations with Vb=0: at Va, (Va-1)/4+Va/4+(Va-0)/2=0, giving Va=0.25 V. The test current is Itest=(1-0.25)/4=0.1875 A, so Zth=1/0.1875=5.333..., rounded to 5.33 Ω.
